newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Winter death toll rises to 43 in Bucharest.
newsitem.headline: Winter death toll rises to 43 in Bucharest.

text.p: About 43 people, mostly homeless, have frozen to death in bitter cold over the past few days in the Romanian capital, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Independent daily Adevarul quoted Bucharest morgue director Vladimir Belis as saying 43 people had frozen to death in Bucharest since Christmas.
Of these, 28 were homeless, Belis told ther paper.
On Sunday, the government said around 20 people had been killed by the cold weather across the country.
"Our morgue has a limited capacity and is overcrowded by the corpses. Cemeteries are refusing to bury therm, saying the soil is frozen and they can't dig graves," Belis said.
Blizzards and snowstorms have swept Romania, disrupting rail, road traffic and shipping. Temperatures reached record lows of minus 25 degrees Celsius ( minus 13F).
On Tuesday, the transport ministry said traffic has resumed on main roads and railways and the main Black Sea port of Constanta, previously closed by gales, had reopened to shipping.
Beggars and homeless people seeking to avoid the big freeze have become a common sight around Romanian railway stations, hotels, restaurants and shops.
